problem: Existing open-vocabulary object navigation and mapping methods work at the semantic-category level, have no instance discrimination module, and cannot update their scene representation when everyday items (e.g. cups) are moved between carriers. This makes efficient navigation to a specific displaced instance hard.
motivation: In homes, frequently used items have unfixed positions and multiple same-category instances, and their carriers (tables, chairs) change. A robot must remember and update scene changes and plan a search strategy under these dynamics. The paper's observation is that small movable objects sit on relatively static carrier furniture, so tracking carried-by relations gives a compact, updatable memory and a good search prior.
key_idea: Build and continuously update an open-vocabulary Carrier-Relationship Scene Graph (carrier furniture vs. carried items), and run a fixed-policy MDP over it that alternates between going to candidate targets ranked by similarity and depth-confidence, and exploring carriers ranked by LLM commonsense.
insight: Updating the CRSG is what makes long-sequence navigation get more efficient: SPL rises with the number of objects for the full method but stays flat for Ours-w/o-update and for VLFM (no memory). Goal determination benefits from all three cues (GPT-4o image comparison, SBERT text similarity, RGB histogram), since removing any one drops SR/Tasks_SR on scene 4. The LLM carrier ranking and the candidate-first policy help too: SPL is 0.205 for random carriers, 0.309 for LLM carriers, and 0.342 for the full strategy.
method: Instance map with captions: builds an open-vocabulary 3D instance map from pre-collected RGB-D, adding to each instance a caption list (Tokenize Anything) and an SBERT text feature alongside the CLIP feature (ConceptGraph-style).

CRSG construction: room/building layers via a prior-based partition; a carrier layer selected by SBERT similarity to 'furniture for holding objects', then GPT-4o filtering of captions, then size and ground-contact filters; a carried layer assigned by a size, distance and xyz-overlap predicate h(O_j,O_i).

Target grounding and determination: text, image (via GPT-4o description) or both are encoded with SBERT to pick the target node; a candidate is accepted by combining SBERT similarity, GPT-4o image-to-image same-object probability, and RGB-histogram cosine similarity.

MDP navigation policy: state (pose, unexplored carriers CR, candidate targets CT, found flag); actions Stop/Explore(cr)/Goto(ct). Candidates are ranked by P_R = w_r*w1*ss*f(d~)/(1+w2*d), with a depth-confidence f (w1=5, w2=1, d1=0.3 m, alpha=10, beta=0.1) and a same-room weight of 0.8 otherwise.

LLM carrier selection: when no candidate exists, GPT-4o receives the captions of unexplored carriers plus the target image/caption and a same-room hint, and picks the carrier most likely to hold the target.

CRSG adaptation: during navigation, CropFormer/TAP/CLIP/SBERT process new RGB frames; observed carriers in the heading half-plane are matched by size, center distance and SBERT similarity, and their carried objects are added, removed or kept. Updates are skipped for partially observed carriers.
Transitions: after each action, carriers seen within radius r with no candidate on them are removed from CR, and stale candidates on them are removed from CT.

setting.backbone: GPT-4o (frozen) with SBERT, CLIP, CropFormer, Tokenize Anything (pretrained, frozen); hand-designed MDP policy
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D with pose (LiDAR SLAM on the real robot); pre-collected RGB-D of the scene for the offline map
setting.action_space: high-level Explore(carrier) / Goto(candidate) / Stop, executed by a local planner to waypoints
setting.simulator: Habitat (Gibson scenes) plus a real robot
setting.privileged: pre-collected RGB-D offline map of the scene built before navigation; simulator poses assumed

numbers.extra: query success on the offline map, not navigation

results: On the 85-query offline map test, the CRSG reaches 82.4% success vs. 52.9% for ConceptGraph and 43.5% for VLMap. In long-sequence navigation across four Gibson scenes, it obtains the highest SR and Tasks_SR(i) against VLFM and OpenFMNav (thresholds 0.4/0.55/0.7); for example, scene 4 SR is 83.3% on the first object where baselines score 0-40%. SPL grows with the number of navigated objects thanks to CRSG updates, and a real-robot demo succeeds on a relocated red book with a gray-book distractor.
limitations: Relies on a pre-built offline map and, for the mapping and decisions, on GPT-4o calls (cost, latency); no active exploration/mapping module, so scalability to unmapped scenes is limited.
Evaluation is small and custom (4 Gibson scenes, 4-5 items each, hand-placed items), with a single-run demonstration on the real robot; SR is 40% in scene 5 for the first object.
Assumes moved objects stay in the same room and that carriers are static; handcrafted thresholds and weights.
